name: Inchiquin

attributes.attribute: a small gray lake on the Burren in County Clare with a magical past
an entry hidden when spring waters rose to form the lake

sources: Kennedy, Patrick. Legendary Fictions of the Irish Celts. (New York: Benjamin Blom, 1969), 282.
Westropp, T. J. Folklore of Clare: A Folklore Survey of County Clare and County Clare FolkTales and Myths. Ennis, Co. Clare: Clasp Press, 2000, pp. 4–5.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Inchiquin is an Irish mythological site. It lies near the town of Corofin on the Burren, a wild rocky part of west County Clare. The small gray Lake of Inchiquin is said to have a magical past. Three beautiful women lived in underground caves there. Each night they came out near a sweet water spring. The lord of the area spied on them and took one for his wife. She bore him several children but made one pledge. He must never bring company home. One night, drunk with friends, he broke the pledge. He found his wife and children leaving for the spring. The waters rose and made the lake of today. They hid the entry to the fairy realm forever.
